Working principle · 3D interactive

How the SME-6300 cleans boards inline

Drag the 3D view to rotate it. Boards travel left to right through three inline units — water-based wash, DI water rinse and hot-air dry — without leaving the line.

WASH
RINSE
DRY
Drag to rotate · scroll to zoom
01 · Water-based wash

Boards enter the wash unit; water-based liquid removes rosin, water-soluble and no-clean flux residues.

02 · DI water rinse

A DI water rinse unit (0–18 MΩ resistivity) clears ionic residue from the board surface.

03 · Hot-air dry

Hot air up to 100 °C dries the board completely before it exits the line.

04 · Back to the line

The clean, dry board continues automatically to the next process — inline, mass production.

The hidden cost of residue and batch cleaning

Uncleaned boards and off-line detours are taxing your line

Every residue-related failure and every board that leaves the line for cleaning costs money. An inline cleaning system changes that math.

Residue left on the board

Flux residue that is not fully removed causes leakage, corrosion and reliability failures in the field.

Batch cleaning breaks the flow

Off-line cleaning means boards leave the line, queue, and come back — killing throughput.

High-end products demand cleanliness

Automotive, medical and industrial electronics require ionic cleanliness that hand or simple washing cannot guarantee.

Manual washing is inconsistent

Hand-cleaning results vary by operator and leave residues in hard-to-reach areas.

Water and detergent waste

Uncontrolled washing consumes DI water and chemistry without predictable results.

Reliability claims without proof

Without a documented cleaning process, field-failure risk stays on your warranty table.

Installation guide

Install and commission the SME-6300

Reference procedure for an inline cleaning machine. Full documentation ships with the machine.

01 · Site preparation

Confirm the footprint (L5200 × W1650 × H1650 mm reference), power (AC 380 V 3-phase 110 kW), DI water supply, air and exhaust at the position.

02 · Line alignment

Align the machine net height (900 ± 25 mm reference) and direction with the adjacent line equipment.

03 · Utilities

Connect power, DI water (6–15 L/min), air (0.5–0.7 MPa) and exhaust (~40 m³/min); fill the clean, pre-rinse and rinse tanks.

04 · Pre-run check

Verify pumps, nozzles and the 1 µm liquid filter; set liquid, DI and dry temperatures for your process.

05 · Test run

Run test boards through wash, rinse and dry; check cleanliness and drying, then release the line.

Technical evaluation FAQ

Questions buyers ask before ordering

What does the SME-6300 clean?

It cleans rosin, water-soluble and no-clean flux residues, plus organic and inorganic contaminants, from assembled PCBA using a water-based process.

How does the inline process work?

Boards travel left to right through three inline units: water-based chemical wash, DI water rinse (0–18 MΩ) and hot-air drying up to 100 °C — all in one pass.

What board sizes can it handle?

PCBA from 50 × 50 mm to 500 × 400 mm, up to 100 mm thick with components, at 0.1–1.5 m/min.

Is it suitable for automotive / medical boards?

Yes — the DI rinse with controlled resistivity (0–18 MΩ) delivers the ionic cleanliness that automotive, medical and industrial electronics require.

What are the facility requirements?

AC 380 V 3-phase 110 kW power, DI water supply 6–15 L/min, air 0.5–0.7 MPa, exhaust about 40 m³/min, and a footprint of about L5200 × W1650 × H1650 mm.

How do I get a price and delivery time?

Email info@smthelp.com or WhatsApp +86 136 0256 2576 with your board details, flux types and volume. Quotation and delivery schedule are provided after technical confirmation — typically the same working day.
